subject: GreenHarbor trial runway relief — SSO/Onboarding snag
messages:
From: Alex Cho <alex.cho@greenharbor.io>

Date: 2027-04-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: GreenHarbor trial runway relief — SSO/Onboarding snag

Hi Marcus,

Quick note from our onboarding team — we hit a blocker integrating GreenHarbor's SSO provider with Redwood's private connector. The engineering team says the adapter is failing during the handshake for a subset of our test users; they're stretched with another client rollout this week.

We're about 6 business days shy of when we need to go live for our pilot, and the sandbox credits are nearly exhausted. Can Redwood provide a short extension plus a small sandbox top-up so our engineers can continue troubleshooting without losing momentum?

We'd like to avoid pushing the pilot timeline but need a runway to finish the SSO fix. If possible: an extra 21 days on the trial window and 100k sandbox token credits would get us past the immediate risk.

I've attached the initial debug bundle the team pulled together (sso_debug_logs.zip). Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks —
Alex
Alex Cho
Platform Lead, GreenHarbor
alex.cho@greenharbor.io
+1 (415) 555-0147

Alex —

Thanks for the note and the logs. Sorry to hear you ran into that handshake failure during onboarding. I looped in Kimberly (engineering liaison) and Naomi (customer success) so we can triage and get you a short-term runway.

Short answers up front: we can provision a temporary sandbox credit top-up and are prepared to extend the trial window pending a quick technical validation. Before I confirm the numbers internally, Kimberly — can you confirm whether the failure pattern in the logs suggests a config mismatch or a compatibility bug? If it's config, we can patch today; if it's a deeper compatibility issue we may need a short dev slot to produce a patch.

Alex — assuming config-level root cause, I can authorize a 21-day extension and 100k sandbox tokens right away. If this looks like a patch needed from our side, I'll propose a 14-day extension with the token top-up and escalate for an engineering hot-fix within 48 hours. Either way, we'll aim to avoid impacting your pilot date.

If you can share the onboarding-checklist.pdf and confirm whether you reproduced the failure on more than one identity provider instance, that will help speed us along.

I'll follow up after Kimberly's read.

Best,
Marcus Lin

Date: 2027-04-10T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GreenHarbor trial runway relief — SSO/Onboarding snag

Hi all —

I dug into sso_debug_logs.zip last night. Summary: the handshake is failing at token validation for a subset of assertions where the NameID format is set to transient; Redwood's connector currently expects persistent NameID for the default mapping. This looks like a config mismatch rather than a code regression — good news for a quick resolve.

Action items I recommend:
- GreenHarbor: If you can configure the IdP to issue persistent NameID for the pilot tenant (or add an attribute mapping equivalent), retry the flow.
- If you cannot change the IdP quickly, we can apply a short-lived mapping override on the sandbox connector to accept transient NameID for the pilot tenant. That requires a brief internal config change (non-code) and a rollback policy post-pilot.

Given this is configuration work, I'm comfortable requesting Marcus approve the 21-day trial extension + 100k sandbox tokens now so your engineers can continue testing while we finalize the quick config path. If GreenHarbor prefers the mapping override route, we'll apply it today and monitor.

Naomi — once Marcus confirms, can you do the approval memo for the extension and note the temporary override option so billing and security have the rollback record?

Kimberly Park
Senior Integration Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Alex / Priya —

All set. Approved: 21-day trial extension from 2027-04-13 through 2027-05-04 and 100,000 sandbox token credit added to your pilot tenant.

Naomi attached an approval memo for records (approval-memo.pdf) and I've pushed the change to HubSpot (link below). If you want us to flip the transient NameID mapping override on the sandbox connector, Kimberly will make that change this afternoon; otherwise update the IdP to persistent NameID as recommended.

Next steps:
- GreenHarbor: confirm whether you'd like the mapping override or IdP change (reply in-thread).
- Redwood: Kimberly will monitor the logs for the next 48 hours and escalate if anything unexpected shows up.
- I'll open a short support ticket to scope a post-pilot hardening plan if you choose the override route.

Thanks for the quick coordination — glad we could get this moving without delaying the pilot.

Regards,
